title: The Blue Lantern

breakdown.title: The Blue Lantern
breakdown.logline: A night bus ride through rain leads to a grandmother's kitchen where a table becomes a boat, carrying the dreamer down a river as a brother waves goodbye with a glowing blue lantern.

words: I was on a night bus with my younger brother, going home through the rain. The bus was almost empty, just the driver and an old woman knitting at the back. My brother was holding a paper lantern with a candle inside it.
It was really coming down. I remember looking out the window and the street lights were melting into long orange ribbons.
He was just sitting there holding the lantern, not really doing anything. The candle light was flickering a bit.
It made the shadows move around a bit, yeah. The old woman knitting at the back didn’t seem to notice.
It felt like I was there, watching from my seat. Like it was really happening.

Then suddenly I was standing in my grandmother’s kitchen, and it was morning. My grandmother was at the stove making tea, and her hair was completely white, whiter than I’ve ever seen it. My brother was there too, still holding the lantern, but now it was glowing blue.
It felt warm and quiet. Normal, almost, except for the blue light. A crowd of neighbours, maybe eight or ten of them, were squeezed into the doorway, watching quietly.
I don’t remember. They were just watching quietly. Could’ve been either.
She was just making tea, like it was any morning. Didn’t turn around or say anything about the neighbours or the lantern.
I just watched. I felt like I couldn’t really speak.
The kitchen table turned into a small wooden boat, and my grandmother told me to get in. That part was strange. She still didn’t look at me. Her voice was calm, like she’d said it a hundred times.
I don’t know… not scared. Just kind of numb. Like I had to do it. So I sat in the boat.

It floated out of the kitchen door and back onto the street where the bus had been, but the street was a river now. My brother waved at me from the bank, still holding the blue lantern. That’s when I woke up.
Sad, but not in a bad way. More like a goodbye that was okay.
It felt solid, like proper wood. It moved really smoothly, like it wasn’t heavy at all.
I don’t remember there being anything else. Just me.
The blue lantern, I think. And my brother’s wave. Those two together.
You got it right. The only thing I’d add is the old woman was knitting at the back of the bus, but that’s all it said. Otherwise that’s exactly it.
Yeah, I think that’s everything I remember.
Yes, I’d like that.
The warm pencil and watercolour one, soft and blended like a memory. That sounds closest to how it felt.
However you imagine me is fine. The dream doesn’t say what I look like, so go with your guess.
That sounds good. I’ll keep an eye out and let you know.

The night bus was almost empty, dim inside, just a few lights and the rain outside. My grandmother’s kitchen was bright morning light, warm and quiet, with neighbours crowded in the doorway. The river street was dark water where the street used to be, like the road had turned into it.
Okay, take your time. I’m interested to see how they come out.
It looks right. Dim and quiet, just like it felt.
It looks right too. Dark water, like the street had fully turned into it.
Yeah, exactly. It’s got that still, quiet pull to it.
It looks close. Just the bright morning light and warm quiet. The neighbours aren’t in the doorway in this one, though.
Okay, that'll make it feel more like the dream.
Yeah, that’s them. Quiet, just watching. It fits.
Okay, I’m curious to see how the lantern comes out, especially the blue glow.
Good, because that blue glow is really the bit that stayed with me.
Yeah, let it do that. It lit the kitchen in a strange way, not harsh, just blue and calm.
Yeah, like a soft blue wash over everything, but the room still felt like morning.
That sounds right. The lantern itself was a normal paper one, but the glow made it feel like the whole kitchen shifted.
It looks right now. The neighbours are in the doorway, the blue glow is there, and it still feels like morning.
Okay, that sounds good. I’ll watch for them as they come.
It looks right. The rain was really coming down, and the lights were turning into those long orange ribbons.
Okay, I’m ready for them.
